study type: Retrospective review and retrospective cohort survey
exposure: Obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) occurrence and grade
Subsequent mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean section)
outcome: Subsequent mode of delivery outcomes (rate of vaginal delivery, rate of caesarean section, recurrent OASI)
Patient satisfaction with mode of delivery
Recall of counselling on future deliveries
cohort: Women who experienced obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) at a tertiary hospital in Australia between 2013-2019 and subsequently had at least one further delivery.
finding: Most women with prior OASI in this unit had subsequent vaginal deliveries and reported high satisfaction rates regardless of delivery mode; there was no statistically significant difference in long-term incontinence scores between those with subsequent vaginal deliveries versus caesarean sections.
mod_finding: Subsequent mode of delivery did not significantly affect long-term incontinence scores, although women with residual EAUS defects were more likely to have caesarean sections, and patient satisfaction was slightly higher in the caesarean section group.
followup_time: 2 to 8 years after the index obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) event.
